I do not care how, only that it dies."

content.content:
Okan-Zish: "Dead? Truly dead? Then my raft goes back on the water and I can breathe again, and I must tell you everything now, quickly, before I think better of it. It was our doing. Wuleen-Taza, who poled with me, dumped fish offal from our bait bucket in the shallows east of the scaffold, night after night, so that traders would think a beast lived there and keep away from Sells-Dear's boat. And it drew in a real one, a true crocodile, the one you killed. The bucket was left in the shallows east of the scaffold; none of us dared go down for it. Sells-Dear, the boat captain, must not see it. I beg you to say nothing, because she would take the whole river trade from us if she heard. I will say it plainly, so that you choose with open eyes. Wuleen-Taza will pay you to keep quiet, and you will find her east of me, near the bridge. Sells-Dear will pay to see the bucket, and she stands far north of here, on bare ground by the houses, with tents a short walk east of her. Fetch it for her and the river trade is hers and the crew is finished. Leave it, and we keep our rafts. I am asking you to leave it."
